title: What is this world?
notes: LORE.md 1c. The towns grew by themselves; the names are a coincidence; a wrong street
name is canon; the calendar is never explained; dilithium lies in wild ground. She
rates the Q theory and never says it was wrong (COMMS.md 6.3). Tier 3 is Tucker Gold
as Shepard told it to her, and only after the channel's GOLD.

lines.text: A copy of Earth that grew up on its own, as far as we can tell.
The same river, the same falls. Towns where the boats have to stop.
They even called it Kentucky. Not every name came out the same.
A wrong street name is on file as a finding, not a mistake.

options.text: Shepard told me who made it.

lines.text: Hodgkin's Law says similar worlds make similar people.
Here somebody seems to have built the laboratory for it.
Starfleet's file says a Q did it. It's a respectable theory.
I rate it. Most sensible people hold it.
Their calendar says 1993. Mine says 2435.
A copy of Earth ought to have kept pace. It didn't.
Shepard checked it four times. Nobody ever explained Miri either.
It lies in open country. Fields and woods. Never in town.
Nobody can tell me why. It's useful, so we use it.
Your tricorder will find it. Your core will thank you.
Holograms, very old. Somebody recorded himself, long ago.
Shepard wants every one of them. So do I, if I'm honest.
She can put each one on tape for the shelf in your cabin.
Bring them to her. In a pocket, they're easy to lose.
Tucker Gold. The man in the recordings.
He copied the land, and the people on it, for one woman.
Then he put the power down and grew old with her.
She's quiet for a moment.
The place was made. The people weren't. Shepard's words, and mine.
